documents.title: Efficacy of Vitamin D Supplementation in Depression in Adults: A Systematic Review
documents.venue: The Journal of Clinical Endocrinology & Metabolism
documents.why_tier: summarises a field rather than adding a measurement

documents.quote: Results of the classical meta-analysis showed no significant effect of Vit D supplementation on postintervention depression scores (standardized mean difference = -0.14, 95% confidence interval = -0.41 to 0.13, P = .32; odds ratio = 0.93, 95% confidence interval = 0.54 to 1.59, P = .79).
documents.verification_scope: Quotation verified, not independent validation of the interpretation.
documents.why: Meta-analysis found no reduction in depression symptoms.

source_fit.method: separate model review; not independent fact-check
source_fit.reason: Meta-analysis of RCTs directly compares vitamin D supplementation vs placebo on depression scores in adults and finds no significant reduction.
